A.biggest_strength: True exploratory interactivity with live continuous sliders for both learning rate and starting position, paired with exact live calculations and side-by-side visual comparison cards.
A.biggest_weakness: Supplementary conceptual notes are slightly more concise than B's extended glossary and optimizer overview.

B.biggest_strength: Comprehensive written supplementary notes covering the second-derivative curvature stability limit, SGD noise, non-convex landscapes, and advanced optimizers.
B.biggest_weakness: Constrained on-rails interactivity limited to three hardcoded presets with no starting point control, paired with compounding roundoff error in the simulation table that wrongly claims the learning rate 'about right lands on 3'.
factual_errors: Claims in Scene 3 that the learning rate 'about right lands on 3' and sets rows 7 and 8 in the table to w=3, g=0, L=0. With η=0.3 on L(w)=(w-3)², gradient descent approaches 3 asymptotically by multiplying distance by 0.4 each step (never reaching 3 in finite steps); the landing on 3 is an artifact of rounding intermediate steps to 2 decimal places and feeding the rounded values into subsequent iterations.
The theoretical contraction recurrence 'each step multiplies the distance to 3 by 1 - 2η' is violated by B's own simulation table after step 2 due to cumulative rounding of intermediate steps.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is the clear winner because it offers a genuine interactive laboratory rather than a scripted slideshow. Students can freely test any learning rate and starting position, watch continuous run/pause animations, inspect an unrounded live data table showing every arithmetic term, and view side-by-side visual comparisons of all three learning rate regimes simultaneously. Furthermore, Page A avoids the mathematical and simulation errors present in Page B, adapts seamlessly to mobile viewports with full label visibility, and supports system light/dark preferences without disruptive autoplay.
